clue.text: Crazy golf brutal? Boy, this is more so!

definitions.text: Crazy golf brutal? Boy, this is more so!

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so the three words that follow are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone finds crazy golf rough, and is told that another ball game is far rougher.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: crazy golf is a gentle miniature-course putting game, and this oval-ball sport is much rougher.
explanation.definitionFit: The contact sport played with an oval ball is famously far rougher than a putting game on a miniature course.

clue.text: Open up novel ruled empty

indicators.note: novel means new or unusual, so the letters of the words before it are put into a fresh order

parts.note: to rule a country is to lead it, so ruled gives led

explanation.surface: Someone opens up a new book of ruled pages only to find it blank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book beside 'ruled' paper, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A place emptied of all its inhabitants is depopulated, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: See 17
Single South African party cuts price, as intended

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the following pieces go inside the word for price

parts.note: a fee is a price charged for a service
single means one, written as the Roman numeral I
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: A South African political party slashes its prices, just as it planned to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' looks like a past participle tied to 'as', but it is the noun: one's intended is one's bride-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's intended is the woman they are engaged to marry, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Speaker's job unclassified?

definitions.meaning: a speaker's work is delivering speeches, making formal addresses
something unclassified has no rating, written as O (nought) followed by RATING

explanation.surface: A question about whether an orator's work counts as a recognised occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: Making formal speeches is precisely what a speaker does; the second sense reads it as zero rating.

clue.text: Unions' privilege to be in disarray, about to secure victory

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the next pieces
in disarray means in a muddle, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: to secure a door is to lock it
V stands for victory, as in the V-sign

explanation.surface: Trade unions' special rights are said to be in chaos, just about to win out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' turns TO BE into BOTE, and 'about' puts it round LOCK and V.
explanation.definitionFit: A block vote lets a union delegate cast all members' votes at once, a privilege unions held at Labour conferences.

clue.text: Grooved without lid, then sealed with clay

indicators.note: a word's lid is its top, so losing the lid removes its first letter

parts.note: a fluted column is grooved with long channels

explanation.surface: An instruction for pottery: cut grooves, take the lid off, then seal with clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without lid' removes F, the first letter of FLUTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints, so luted means sealed in that way.

clue.text: Suck on this, Chuck, then pickle sweet food

parts.note: a straw is what you suck a drink through
Chuck Berry was the American rock and roll guitarist and singer
a pickle is a fix or tight spot, as is a jam

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to suck on something, then a sweet treat in a pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a verb meaning throw; it is the singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve of boiled fruit and sugar spread on bread is a sweet food.

clue.text: Did Ian Paisley promise to in Bond film?

definitions.text: Did Ian Paisley promise to in Bond film?

parts.words: Did Ian Paisley promise to in Bond film?
parts.note: Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish unionist leader, was famous for shouting his one-word refusal; promising to repeat that refusal once more names a 1983 Sean Connery spy film

explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley led Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionists and was known for his cry of 'Never!' to any compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the 1983 James Bond film that brought Sean Connery back to the role.

clue.text: 15 on hand?

parts.note: 15 is the clue for a star performer; a hand is a bunch of bananas, and the fruit at its top would be the chief one

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the leading person, the boss or star of a show, which matches the cross-referenced headline act.

clue.text: See 17
A fight is on

parts.note: a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: A boxing contest is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is on' reads as 'is happening'; 'on' alone is the definition in its sense of concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A book on birds concerns birds, so on and this word are synonyms meaning concerning.

clue.text: Elegant spirit, river bird

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
the ka was the spirit or soul in ancient Egyptian belief
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: An elegant ghostly bird seen on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: KA is the ancient Egyptian life spirit, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A small North American songbird of the tit family is called by this name.

clue.text: Temperamental socialist?

definitions.meaning: a Bolshevik, the Russian revolutionary socialist, shortened

explanation.surface: Is a moody person a left-winger?
explanation.definitionFit: British informal for awkward and uncooperative; it is also a shortening of Bolshevik.

clue.text: Male psychiatrist commits popular star performer

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: to commit someone is to shut them in, so the psychiatrist's name holds the next piece

parts.note: Alfred Adler was the Austrian psychiatrist who founded individual psychology
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A male psychiatrist has a well-known star committed to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commits' reads as doing something; here it means confining someone, as to a hospital, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The top-billed act at a concert or festival is the star turn whose name heads the poster.

clue.text: Part of throat needing good fortune to settle back

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or fortune

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the word for settle is read in reverse

parts.note: to settle into a chair is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore throat needs luck for it to settle down again.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening between the vocal cords in the larynx is the anatomical name for this part of the throat.

clue.text: Satanic how it is?

parts.note: Satan is the ... of Revelation, so how he is, his essential character

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means the inherent character of something; read literally it describes the Devil, the Beast of Revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the essential or unavoidable character of a thing, which is how it is.

clue.text: Socialist record, bureaucracy

parts.note: red is the colour of socialism, and a Red is a socialist
to tape something is to record it

explanation.surface: A left-winger's record of dealing with officialdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive official rules and form-filling are known by this name, from the ribbon tying documents.

clue.text: I bore myself standing for those having left office

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means upright, so all the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to bore someone is to tire them
me is the speaker referring to themself

explanation.surface: A retiree confesses that being on their feet all day bores them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns I TIRE ME upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired professors and officials who keep their title honorarily are given this plural Latin name.

clue.text: Question about beer brewed via that method

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the question word goes round the following letters

parts.note: why is a question word

indicators.note: brewed means mixed and fermented, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query about how beer is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Question' gives the single word asked, not a general query; 'via that method' is the formal adverb sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This formal adverb means by which, or through which means something happens.

clue.text: Used to be time in central area for cleaning vessel

parts.note: was is the past tense of be

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a hub is the centre of activity

explanation.surface: Once upon a time a central space held a bath for washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tub used for laundry is a vessel for cleaning clothes.

clue.text: Party echoing among loud voices — Alpine ones

indicators.note: among means in the middle of, so the reversed party goes inside the shouters

parts.note: yellers are people with loud voices who shout

indicators.note: an echo comes back, so the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party's noise rings out among loud singers in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpine ones' refers back to the loud voices, so the definition is people who sing in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singers who warble between falsetto and chest voice are the classic mountain singers.

clue.text: In homicide, a throttling heralds this

definitions.text: In homicide, a throttling heralds this

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a murder, strangling comes before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'homicide, a throttling'; the whole clue also defines, since strangling leads to dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Throttling someone in a killing leads to the end of life.

clue.text: Here's one small step

parts.note: the phrase recalls the moonwalk, while a single tap on a keyboard bar moves the cursor a small step

explanation.definitionFit: A gap between typed words is one small step along the line; also the realm of astronauts.

clue.text: One tucked in bed's getting up — might he seem cold?

indicators.note: tucked in means placed snugly inside, so the numeral goes into the beds
in a down clue, getting up means rising, so the beds are read from the bottom up

parts.note: bed's is read as beds, plural, and cots are beds
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone tucked up in bed rises in the morning, looking chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns COTS into STOC, and 'tucked in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Greek school of endurance shows no emotion, so seems cold and unfeeling.

clue.text: See 9
Breakdown in reduction is present

indicators.note: a breakdown splits something apart, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slump in reductions is current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' is the verb, as in presenting one person to another.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone to a guest is to make them known, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: He won something sweet, far more than a can of coke!

parts.note: charlie is slang for cocaine
a bucket holds much more than a can

explanation.surface: A winner of a sweet prize is told a can of cola is nothing compared to what he got.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls Roald Dahl's boy who won the factory in Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy hero who wins Willy Wonka's chocolate factory in Roald Dahl's novel.
